chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two (peace be upon them), who said:

When a man finds a stray sacrificial animal, he should announce it on the day of sacrifice, the second day, and the third day; then he should slaughter it on behalf of its owner on the evening of the third day.

And he (peace be upon him) said regarding a man who sends the obligatory sacrificial animal, but the animal perishes in the road before it reaches its destination, and he has no capacity to send another: Allah (Glorious is He) is the Foremost with the excuse, unless he knows that when he asks (for a replacement) he will be given it.

key_terms.أَوْلَى بِالْعُذْرِ: More deserving of the excuse (i.e., God accepts the excuse readily)
key_terms.هَدْياً: Sacrificial animal (usually for Hajj or Umrah)
key_terms.يُعَرِّفْهُ: To announce or make known (to the people)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a sacrificial animal gets lost or dies before reaching its destination?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the jurisprudence of stray sacrificial animals (hady), specifying a three-day announcement period before the finder slaughters it on the owner's behalf, reflecting the practical application of Hajj rituals. It further clarifies the condition of 'excuse' (udhr) for those whose sacrificial animal perishes in transit, noting that exemption from providing a replacement applies unless the individual knows that requesting one would be granted, a nuance highlighted by Shia scholars regarding certainty versus probability.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Al A’ala Bin Razeyn, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, 
(It has been narrated) from one of the two<sup>asws</sup> (5<sup>th</sup> or 6<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>) having said:

‘When the man finds a stray sacrificial animal, so he should introduce it (to the people) on the day of the sacrifice, and the second day, and the third day. Then he should slaughter it on behalf of its owner on the evening of the third (day)’.

And he<sup>asws</sup> said regarding the man who sends the Obligatory sacrificial animal, but the animal perishes in the road before it reaches (the place of sacrifice), and there is no capacity for him that he would (get another) sacrificial animal’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, Glorious is He<sup>azwj</sup>, is the Foremost with the (Accepting of the) excuse, except if he happens to know that when he asks (for a replacement) he would be given it’.
en.sarwar: 5. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan ibn Yahya from al-‘Ala’ ibn Razin from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following: “One of the two Imam, (abu Ja’far or abu ‘Abd Allah), ‘Alayhim al-Salam, has said, ‘

If one finds a lost offering animal, he must make a public announcement. He can do so on the day of al-Nahr (slaughtering the offering, 10th of Dhu al-Hajjah). On the second day and on the third day, then slaughter it on behalf of its owner in the evening of the third day.’

About a man who sends an obligatory offering and it is destroyed on the way before reaching its place and he is not able to replace it, he (the Imam) said, ‘Allah, most Glorious, is the first to accept his excuse, unless he knows that if he asks he is given his wish.’”
